newsitem.title: SWEDEN: BALTICS - BANKERS TRUST SEES MORE GDRS FROM REGION.
newsitem.headline: BALTICS - BANKERS TRUST SEES MORE GDRS FROM REGION.

text.p: The Bankers Trust Company said on Thursday that it saw more global depository receipts (GDRs) coming out of the Baltic region as local companies seek more varied and flexible ways to raise capital from abroad.

"I think we will see GDRs from all three Baltic countries this year," Avarina Miller, a vice president with Bankers Trust Company, told Reuters at a Baltic capital markets and investment conference held in the Swedish capital.
She added that they would probably come from different sectors and that the privatisation process would boost the number of GDRs offered.
"The Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA) makes no secret of the fact that it wants companies being privatised to raise capital through GDRs," she said.
"The LPA has an aggressive time table and it is looking at selling off several big companies," she added.
Lithuania's Vilniaus Bank issued the first Baltic GDR last year, raising $17.1 million in the process. Its GDRs are traded on the Luxembourg bourse.
Lithuania's Birzai Dairy followed with a $6 million issue which was privately placed and not listed.
Miller said GDRs not only helped individual companies but helped draw investor attention to the entire regional market.
